description.p: Whatevr is a native Linux WhatsApp client backed by the whatevrd background daemon.

Opening a channel now pulls its latest posts from the server through the new channel.messages_refresh command and stores the unseen ones, so muted channels — which rarely get pushes — show what is there. Fetched posts carry the same ids as pushes and store once.
Tapping another channel in the list now resubscribes instead of keeping the previous channel's posts behind the new header; reopening the same channel is a no-op.

p.em: Channel invite links open in place

description.p: Tapping a whatsapp.com/channel/<invite>[/<post>] link in any message resolves the channel without following it (new channel.resolve_invite query), opens its timeline, and scrolls the linked post into view once its row arrives.

The phone's address book is now searchable. search.chats answers matching saved contacts beside the chat rows, in a Contacts section after Chats, and a new contacts view lists the whole address book in saved-name order for browsing. Tapping one starts the chat through the existing chat.ensure_direct, so its row arrives through the chats view like any other new chat. A number that is not saved still resolves through the phone lookup as before.

Pasting an image now stages it in the attachment dialog instead of sending immediately, so pasted images get the same caption and basic edits (crop, rotate, draw) as attached and dropped files. Nothing leaves the device until Send is pressed.
The daemon cross-compiles for Windows again: build-tagged portability shims for the platform-specific pieces and a working libjpeg-turbo lookup for the thumbnail decoder.

ul.li: Protocol client lifecycle: subscription lists are copied before reset and re-subscribe walks, closing use-after-free and skipped-subscription windows on reconnect races.
View updates re-check sink liveness on every change, so a handler that evicts a window mid-update cannot be called after free.
Subscribe responses without a subscription id no longer register a colliding id-0 route; the subscription fails loudly instead.
Socket short writes now fail the connection instead of silently desynchronizing the frame stream.
Pre-hello queue failures are async like every other failure path.
Stale-subscription cleanup checks id presence instead of stringifying the value, so numeric ids actually unsubscribe.
event.rsvp with an unknown response fails fast instead of sending UNSPECIFIED.
Negative subscribe limits are clamped instead of wrapping on the wire.

Daemon: unchecked history-notification type assertion, poison group ids retried forever, wiped preferences lost silently on read error, per-typist timer pileup, hung requests on closing connections, live-row scan errors, history slice aliasing, monotonic fold sequence, corrupt fold checkpoints, singleton chat-view id churn, empty send sequences, and CLI hangs on out-of-band errors.
Unread sidebar filter works again via a local proxy over the all subscription; failed subscribes settle instead of spinning.
Multi-file sends go out as sequential send.media requests; send.media_batch quality is dropped (no v2 field).
The startup status mode shows a neutral splash, not the stories StatusPage; the Status tab remains on the rail.
Channel posts use the same ProtocolMessageModel + ChatBubble presentation as conversations, so images/video load and open in the normal viewers.
Typing indicators are a frontend-local setting (no v2 preference field); anti-delete, keep-archived, and archived-mute toggles are disabled with notes until the daemon grows those preferences.
Tray right-click is the native menu (Show/Hide, notifications mute, Quit); the QML menu had positioning bugs.
privacy.set value none canonicalizes to nobody; search sticker results use the library row shape; message sticker rows carry the library key for favorite/download actions.
Sync type/phase map to the v1 vocabulary the strip renders.

Restored v1 preferences on protocol 2 (new Preferences/PreferencesSet fields): archived-mute (daemon notifier skips archived chats), anti-delete (revoke tombstones keep content with the Deleted mark), keep-archived (appstate unarchives dropped at ingest).
New LogsView/LogRow over the daemon run log plus log_message command (restores the Logs tab and frontend log forwarding).
New ChatLinksView: the gallery Links tab lists link-carrying messages again.
Chat folders (chat_folders view, chat_folder.* commands, folder filter on chats).
Favorites filter and per-chat favorite (chat.favorite, device-local like pins).
Status/stories (feed and muted views, post text/media, viewed flags, mutes, replies, viewers, delete).
Calls and call history (ringing set from the call log, call.reject).
Channels (directory and local message views with media, follow/unfollow/mute/viewed/react/refresh; server ids retained for viewed/react).
Groups and communities (create, invite links, members, photo, announce/locked, link/unlink).
Schedules (schedule.text/list/cancel with a daemon-side due sender).
Backups (daemon.backup_export, keyring passphrase) and daemon.shutdown.
Sends (send.poll/contact/location/cancel), chat.mark_all_read, chat.export, media.save, message.edit_history (bodies retained from this update on), privacy.set_default_timer.
send.media_batch on the daemon (Qt sends multi-file sequentially instead).
group.join_link and community.subgroups (no frontend calls them yet).
Status text background/font styling (received and stored, but Qt never rendered it).
Media byte counters.
Merge upstream: new v2 core daemon (core/model/ingest/live/views/server), protocol 2 protobuf framing, frontend registry with default-frontend and terminal setting, macOS app and Homebrew packaging.
Qt frontend ported to protocol 2 behind a JSON-compatibility shim: same UI, same suites — Go 17/17 packages and Qt 11/11 tests pass, including new v2 frame-codec and shim unit tests.
Frontend-owned tray icon (StatusNotifierItem) with toggle, menu, and quit; the v2 daemon exports no tray of its own.
Forward-to picker now lists archived chats alongside active ones.
CI gains a Qt frontend job (Arch build, offscreen tests, install-tree artifact); AGENTS.md documents the CI-first build policy and artifact install flow.
Multi-file sends go out as sequential send.media requests; protocol 2 has no batch command and no quality field.
Group creation and other v1-only surface (folders, status, calls, channels, logs, chat links, schedules, backups, disappearing-timer default) report unknown_method until the daemon grows those APIs.
privacy.set value none canonicalizes to nobody on the wire.
The v2 daemon keeps its WhatsApp session in a new store: scan the QR to re-pair after upgrading from a v1 daemon; the old login does not transfer.
Add a default-on setting to mute notifications from archived chats, covering messages, calls, and reactions.
Replace the indefinite startup connection spinner with a retryable error after a brief loading state.
Clamp tray menu placement to screen geometry and open upward when space allows; Wayland compositors may override placement.

just install now actually replaces a running frontend. The restart step matched ^$prefix/bin/whatkevr$, but a frontend cold-started from the tray runs as whatkevr whatevr:// and a pop-out window as whatkevr --new-window …. Neither matched, so the old process survived, the newly launched one handed its activation to the old one and exited single-instance, and the install completed successfully while changing nothing. Since a tray cold start goes through xdg-open whatevr://, this was the ordinary path, not an edge case: the install would report success and the old build would keep running. Only the trailing anchor is gone — the leading one is what stops the recipe from killing its own shell, and it was the trailing one that was doing the damage.

A failed QML root object now says so. If the QML root cannot be created the app exited 1 having printed nothing, because Qt's own diagnostic does not always reach stderr. That silence is why a one-line QML mistake once took four builds to track down.

Fixes a regression from 0.11.3. The offline media gate shipped with a Connections block so that bubbles parked while offline would start fetching again on reconnect. A Connections block is one QObject per delegate, and the chat bubble has a hard object budget per row, so all of the budget checks failed by exactly one object. The gate now lives in the autoDownloadWanted property, which already had a change handler and already reads the connection phase — so reconnecting restarts those bubbles just the same, and the delegate costs nothing extra.

Opening the Logs tab no longer builds the whole log. It subscribed with limit: 1000, so the daemon materialised its entire ring into rows on the first tick. The page now asks for a recent window, which is the view's own default. Older history is in the rotated file that "Open folder" opens.

Clicking the tray icon no longer re-raises a window that is already up. activateWindow() ran show + raise + requestActivate unconditionally — three round trips to the compositor — and the icon's Activate arrives several times a second at the same coordinates. The sequence is now skipped when the window is already visible and focused. A window parked to the tray still raises, because visible is false while it is hidden.

No more media requests while the client is offline. Auto-downloading asked the daemon for bytes with no connection to serve them; the daemon failed each one instantly, and because a bubble only arms its latch after asking — and resets it when the delegate is reused — every recycled bubble asked again. That was the flood of media.download … WhatsApp is not connected in the log. Requests are now gated on the connection phase, and the latch is left unarmed on that path so reconnecting starts the bubbles again rather than silently leaving them unfetched.

Left-clicking the tray icon opens the window again. The status-notifier item advertised ItemIsMenu: true, which tells the panel "this icon is a menu: a click should open the menu, not activate the application". The panel then never called Activate at all, so a left-click did nothing — and since the item exports no com.canonical.dbusmenu for the panel to render, there was no menu on that click either. The daemon log made it plain: 44 right-clicks (ContextMenu), zero Activate. It is now false, which is the standard split the app was written against: left-click raises the window, right-click opens the tray menu.

Qt and QML warnings now show up in the Logs tab. They only ever reached the frontend's stderr, so a warning in the running app was invisible unless you happened to be watching a terminal — which is exactly what the Logs tab is for. Diagnostics are now forwarded to the daemon over a new daemon.log command and land in the same in-memory ring the Logs page already tails, prefixed frontend: so the two sources stay tellable apart. Severity is still inferred from the message text, so a QML MouseArea: line renders as a warning and an mpv failure as an error.

The media viewer's circular hit area works. MediaViewer.qml gave its containmentMask an untyped contains(point). Qt looks the mask up by the exact signature contains(QPointF); an untyped QML function registers as taking a QVariant, so Qt ignored the mask and logged Object set as mask does not have an invokable contains method. The mask is now typed, which is what actually makes a round video note ignore its own corners instead of playing and pausing from the backdrop around it. ChatBubble.qml already declared its types and had this right.

Right-clicking the tray icon shows the menu, and not the main window. The handler was calling root.show() before it showed its own menu, so the first thing the icon did was raise the whole app. That is exactly what a right-click should not do: the app underneath is left alone and a three-row menu (Minimize to tray / Disable notifications / Quit) appears where the pointer was. This is the shape of Telegram's tray menu, in phrasing, not just in looks.

The tray menu window is no longer a 1×1 dot. Its size was bound to a plain Rectangle's implicitWidth/implicitHeight, which is always zero, so it mapped at 0.8×0.8 before it even got a chance to render. It computes its size from the button content now.

The tray menu now reads like Telegram's. tdesktop's rebuildMenu is three rows: a show/hide row whose label follows the window state, one notification toggle phrased as the action it performs, then Quit. Ours had two checkboxes both writing notifications_enabled, so they could show contradictory states, and no way to hide the window from the menu at all.

whattui can finally act on a chat. It was calling 9 of the 83 commands in PROTOCOL.md. Pin, mute, archive, favourite, block, mark read and mark all read are wired now, plus a right-click context menu over a chat row that acts on that row rather than on whichever chat happens to be open.

Merged upstream main whole, bringing the terminal frontend up to date: whatevrd pair for linking a phone from any terminal, parked edits and revokes that survive a message arriving late, edit_until so a frontend stops offering an edit the daemon will refuse, and a long tail of whattui rendering fixes.

The tray menu leads with a Show Whatevr / Minimize to tray row driven by the window's real state, and its notification toggle is a single button labelled with the action it performs, hidden while the app-lock PIN is up.

whattui chat actions: chat.pin, chat.mute, chat.archive, chat.favorite, contact.block, chat.mark_read and chat.mark_all_read. Each is a registry command, so each is a palette row and a slash command too.
whattui right-clicks a chat row for a context menu over that chat, with each toggle labelled with what pressing it will do — Unpin chat over a chat that is already pinned.
whatevrd pair, so a phone can be linked from any terminal without starting a frontend.
The daemon now tells frontends when a message stops being editable, and parks an edit or revoke that outran its message instead of dropping it.

Four tray icons where there should be one. A StatusNotifierItem registration is the watcher's to keep — nothing takes it back when the process dies — so every whattui golden-frame run left its mock daemon's icon in the panel permanently. A mock daemon now stays off the session bus entirely, the way it already stayed off notifications.

An edit or revoke that arrived before its message was parked and replayed rather than lost. Dropping one is not cosmetic: nothing ever says it again, so a message somebody deleted for everybody stayed in the transcript for good.
The account's maps are emptied on logout and every view re-reads the store after it, rather than the maps being taken away underneath them.
Stars an account already had are applied on connect.
A captioned message's one-line summary says what the message is rather than what it says, which is the line WhatsApp itself shows.

The README feature map now says it is a map of the daemon, and feature-gap.md tracks the frontend gaps per frontend — including the whattui work still owed and the features deliberately not ported to a terminal.

description.p: Received photos and videos can be turned in the full-screen viewer, and attachments can be edited before they are sent.

ul.li: Turn a photo or a clip in the full-screen viewer, with toolbar buttons, R and Shift+R, and a reset. Turning is a view change: it costs nothing, and the alternative for a sideways photo is turning the device. A clip is a framebuffer item, so it follows the same rotation a photo does.

Drag to reposition a zoomed picture, and the clamp that stops you dragging it off screen now measures the rotated box. That was wrong: a zoomed photo turned on its side could previously be dragged until it left the viewport.

Cycle through every photo and clip in a chat. This already worked, with one gap: pictures sent together in an album were unreachable from the walk, because it keyed on the album row's own album kind and stepped over its tiles. Album tiles are now expanded in the album's place, so they keep the order they were sent in.

A quarter turn, a crop and a freehand mark on a photo, and a quarter turn on a clip. The picked file is never modified — the edit is baked into a new file in the cache and that is what gets staged in its place, so cancelling costs a quarter turn and a squiggle rather than the original.
Standard or HD for the whole batch, from the send dialog. A standard photo is held to 1600px the way official clients send them, and a standard clip to 1280px. HD sends the original bytes.

description.p: Crop, rotate, mirror and undo come from KQuickImageEditor (invent.kde.org/libraries/kquickimageeditor) — KDE's own, already part of the Plasma stack this app is built on, licensed like the Kirigami it sits beside, and what NeoChat and Photos use for the same job. Only the pen is ours, because its annotation system composites onto a fixed canvas rather than recomposing one, which is the wrong model for editing a photo to send.

ul.li: send.media_batch takes a quality parameter (standard or hd) and now reaches the frontend's Standard/HD control. quality was already implemented on the daemon for send.media but was unreachable from the UI.
Both send.media_batch and the quality parameter are documented in PROTOCOL.md, which neither was. The additive changes keep the protocol at version 1.

description.p: A clip re-encode needs ffmpeg. It is optional and best-effort exactly as the daemon's poster frames already are: with no ffmpeg on PATH, a standard clip is sent as it is rather than not being sent.

p.em: Statuses now expire after 24 hours, for real

description.p: Nothing ever deleted an old status. The prune function existed but had no callers, so the database kept every status it had ever seen, and the per-contact Keep toggle archived the expired ones on top of that.

The daemon now prunes on connect and after every ingest: the rows, the cached media and thumbnails behind them, and the view receipts that pointed at them. A status lives exactly as long as it does on the phone.

Status had two entry points: the left-rail Status tab, and a horizontal contact-name strip across the top of the viewer. The strip is gone. Skipping between contacts still works through the viewer's previous/next-contact buttons and their keyboard shortcuts.

The per-contact Keep (archive) toggle, and with it the Status tab's Archived section, the status.kept view and the status.keep_sender command. With retention fixed at the 24 hour status life there was nothing left for it to archive. This narrows the protocol rather than extending it, so frontends have to be updated alongside the daemon.

whatevrd parsed its flags before it registered the mock ones, so --mock was rejected as an undefined flag in mock builds, and a release build reported Go's "flag provided but not defined" rather than the rebuild hint. That failed CI twice over: the mock-gate check wanted the hint, and the whattui golden-frame tests started a mock daemon that exited immediately, so they waited out their startup deadline and the suite timed out.
Groups become writable, and the Calls tab grows a history.

ul.li: Create a group from the chat-list header, with a multi-select member picker.

Group admin controls on the group card: edit subject and description, change or clear the photo, toggle admins-only sending and admins-only info editing, add participants, and per-member make admin, dismiss admin, remove.
The composer is disabled with an explanation in an admins-only group, instead of letting the send fail server-side.

Call history: a new call_history view lists every logged call across chats, and the Calls tab renders it under the ringing section with direction, video/voice, duration and timestamp. Tapping a row opens the chat.
Communities: the group card shows the community's linked groups, with link and unlink for admins.

Chat lists ("Lists") can be created, renamed and deleted, not only assigned. The Archived header carries an unread badge and shows the "these chats stay archived when new messages are received" notice.
An Accessibility page: increase contrast (applied to the palette) and reduce motion, which really stops GIF, animated-sticker and GIF-status autoplay.
Status audience privacy row, a default disappearing-message timer (off / 24 hours / 7 days / 90 days), and a keep chats archived preference so archived chats stop resurfacing on a new message.
The status viewer gets a clickable contact-name strip, so moving to another person's statuses needs no close button.
Backup, keyring and app-lock passphrases were echoed in cleartext: the echoMode binding named a type that does not exist, so the binding threw and the fields fell back to plain text.
The status viewer could hang on a second still status, because the auto-advance timer hung off a boolean that does not change between two stills.
The chat_folders view rejected the view parameter every client sends, so the list rail could never subscribe and folders were permanently invisible.
Thirteen list views turned one transient store read failure into an empty answer, which made the client delete every row it was holding.
chat.mark_all_read cleared badges for archived and badge-only chats without publishing the change, so those badges never cleared.
The notification worker blocked its whole queue on an unbounded WhatsApp round trip, and send.media ran inline on the protocol read loop, stalling every other request behind a 2 GiB read.
A call left ringing survived logout and came back as a phantom incoming call after the next login.
Hidden album children counted toward the unread badge but not toward the unread anchor, so opening at "unread" could land on already-read history.

Sticker bubbles never drew their in-progress placeholder; switching settings categories never collapsed a drill-in page; the secondary workspace tabs had no title; the app-lock PIN was not focused when the lock screen appeared after startup.

description.p: Upstream codelif/whatevr: the whattui terminal frontend, the wamock fake WhatsApp server for frontend development, and six daemon fixes (seconds-not-milliseconds message timestamps, unread messages arriving mid history-sync, the no-session-bus crash, whitespace-only text, an avatar-refresh race, and push-name precedence over address book names), plus a whatsmeow bump.
The protocol stays at version 1: every addition is new, nothing changed shape.

Forwarded-message header borrowed from Telegram Desktop (bubbles show a Forwarded header; doc/tdesktop-notes.md adds the full whatkevr-vs-tdesktop verdict table). Inbound stickers now enter Recents, and the sticker picker stays open for multi-send like WhatsApp mobile (plain click sends and keeps it open, Ctrl+click closes).

p.em:
Whatevr 0.8.7

Desktop parity and workspace improvements.

## Highlights

- Persistent two-column workspace for chats, status, calls, channels, logs, and starred messages.
- Mobile-style status autoplay with embedded video playback, timed stills, and next-person progression.
- Desktop microphone voice recording through Qt Multimedia and the existing voice send path.
- Durable one-shot scheduled text messages.
- Local chat favorites and daemon-owned custom chat folders.
- Channel message loading, viewed receipts, and reactions.
- Message Info sent, delivered, read, and played details.
- Notification mark-read and capability-gated inline reply actions.
- Expanded tray menu and right-click actions.
- Frontend app lock and backup controls.

GIF provider search, multi-account support, live SQLCipher encryption, and full desktop call media remain deferred.

ul.li: Chat export: "Export chat…" in the conversation menu writes the transcript (.txt, official export shape with timestamps, names, markup, media markers) through a save dialog.
Document sends keep their real filenames end to end (regression-tested).
Tray menu is a real popup window at the click point; the icon never pulses.
Channel pages load older messages on scroll.
Status viewer refreshes the moment downloads land.
scripts/verify_features.py: local checks for every README feature row.

description.p: Screenshot-driven fixes plus the tray/status/notification follow-through.

ul.li: Logs tab actually fills now (rows carry ids), with copy actions and an open-log-folder button.
Chat media gallery filters work again, and Channels refreshes on open.
Status rings on chat avatars with tap-to-view, thumbnail avatars in the status list, and auto-download when a status opens.
Tray right-click menu fixed, unread tooltip corrected, channel posts notify, misfiled newsletter chats purged and blocked from returning.

Plus the extra-features batch: anti-delete, edit history, status keep and archive, sender client indicator, unread filter, pop-out windows, typing toggle, multi-file attach, markup shortcuts, @admins, and a new doc/ folder with build, safety, and troubleshooting guides.

description.p: Screenshot-driven fixes plus the tray/status/notification follow-through.

ul.li: Logs tab actually fills now (rows carry ids), with copy actions and an open-log-folder button.
Chat media gallery filters work again, and Channels refreshes on open.
Status rings on chat avatars with tap-to-view, thumbnail avatars in the status list, and auto-download when a status opens.
Tray right-click menu fixed, unread tooltip corrected, channel posts notify, misfiled newsletter chats purged and blocked from returning.

Plus the extra-features batch: anti-delete, edit history, status keep and archive, sender client indicator, unread filter, pop-out windows, typing toggle, multi-file attach, markup shortcuts, @admins, and a new doc/ folder with build, safety, and troubleshooting guides.

description.p: Statuses, tray follow-ups, and everyday sending improvements on top of 0.8.1.

ul.li: The status@broadcast chat is back: statuses are filed there as ordinary messages alongside the Status tab, silently — no unread bump, no notification. Disable it in Settings, Chats, Status.
Old statuses gain their thumbnails automatically on connect, and video statuses now play in the viewer.
Drop files onto a conversation to send them.
Saving a profile picture prefills the chat or contact name.
The Logs page reports load failures instead of staying blank.

description.p: Fix release on top of 0.8.0: the Logs tab, status thumbnails, and the tray icon all work now.

ul.li: The Logs tab was always empty because only the command existed, not the view. The daemon.logs view now streams recent log lines into the page.
Statuses render thumbnail-first: sender thumbnails are cached at ingest, and opening a status auto-downloads the full media.
Tray left-click raises the window; right-click shows a menu with Open, a Notifications toggle, and Quit. The icon pulses only while unread chats exist.
Status rows show sender avatars instead of initials-only, and the profile-picture viewer gained a Save button.
Fixed a non-idempotent database migration, a missing import, and the chat-bubble performance test's properties and budgets.
whatsmeow pinned to the 2026-09-15 commit; no API changes.

Fixed a launch-blocking bug: since the last release the frontend failed to open at all — one QML file used a qualified QQC2.Button without its import, which made the whole interface fail to load. Whatevr now starts.
The expression picker no longer freezes on the stickers tab when switching back to emoji or closing the picker.
Sending: video, audio, voice notes and documents (not just images), view-once sending, quoted replies and caption edits for all media, and attaching any file type.
New Status tab: post text/photo/video/audio statuses, view contacts statuses with a stepped viewer, download and save them.
Calls tab: incoming 1:1 and group calls ring with a desktop notification (answer on your phone), call rejection, and missed-call tombstones.
Groups and communities: create, leave, rename, topic, photo, invite links, join by link, member management, announce/lock settings, and community sub-groups with admin link/unlink.
Backups: AES-256-GCM encrypted export bundles, offline whatevrd --restore import, and backup passphrase storage in the OS keyring (Secret Service).
Media saving: copy any chat media, status, or profile photo to a path of your choice; inbound view-once media can be saved on demand.
Polls, channels, contacts, locations and a daemon log viewer in the frontend.
Tray icon with connection state and unread indicator, rotated debug log file, and a daemon.logs query over the in-memory ring.

p.em: gRPC is dead. Long live the daemon!

description.p: After almost 2 months of work, Whatevr finally has the architecture I wanted from the start.
New stuff:

ul.li: whatkevr now talks to whatevrd over a stable, documented local protocol. One daemon, one socket, and as many frontends as you want.
Two tiny example frontends now ship with the project, including a working WhatsApp client in about 30 lines of shell.
Phone-side chat deletions and read state now sync properly, and Whatevr can ask the phone for older history.
You can edit your profile about, block contacts, open downloaded photos in the viewer, and see useful tombstones for unsupported media.
Added a setting to snap back to the newest message after sending.

description.p: Fixed stuff:

ul.li: Chats open much faster, the chat list loads lazily, and navigation and column slides are considerably smoother.
Unread counts can actually be cleared now, unread dividers land where they should, and new-message badges no longer count your own sends.
Starred messages, search results, reply quotes, and other message jumps now go to the correct message instead of vaguely opening the chat.
Fixed animated stickers turning into blocky garbage after the first frame.
Fixed custom wallpapers appearing squashed or missing while opening a chat.
Fixed encrypted message edits, changed contact identities, stalled history syncs, and several "waiting for this message" cases.
Lots of protocol hardening, ordering fixes, UI polish and regression tests.

description.p: Upgrade note:
The systemd socket moved in this release. If you use the systemd user units, run:

p.code: systemctl --user daemon-reload systemctl --user try-restart whatevrd.socket whatevrd.service See ya! I am going to stare at something that is not a socket now.

description.p: New stuff:

ul.li: Fully customizable doodle wallpaper (inbuilt + bring your own doodle)
Can enable notification sounds

description.p: Fixed stuff:

ul.li: Bubble geometry follows font size
search settings won't activate first option and show weird states now
Auto downloads now downloads based on what is visible instead of downloading every incoming media

description.p: Small release, but really close to my heart. See ya!
Well look who decided it would be a great idea to leave -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE to DEBUG
Yeah, me. Well that gave me an excuse to iron out some things so win-win

ul.li: moved root Makefile to a justfile, its cleaner
fixed some cmake and compiler warnings
changed the release markdown renderer so it now supports a bigger subset of the spec (I can add links (youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ))

description.p: See ya next time! (no one is reading these)
New stuff:

ul.li: Closing a chat with non-empty composer will leave it as a draft
You can edit sent message and received messages will be edited (no more fun)
Messages can be pinned and they show up on top of the chat
You can star/unstar and see starred messages (global and chat-wise)
Archived chats
Mute chats
Search (wow), you can search contacts and messages and both
There is a quick side bar with home, groups, DMs and Starred messages, settings and profile buttons
Wait whaaaaa!! SETTINGS!!! HELL YEAHH!!! BASIC FEATURES IN 2026!
Tags are now expanded, so you'll actuall see @Ma Home Boi instead of @453243mumbojumbo in chat

description.p: Fixed stuff:

ul.li: Read more now shows a dialog box instead of changing the chat geometry
Clear composer after sending media
Clicks were leaking through avatar in contact info
smol fixes and perf improvements

description.p: I react to Context Menus Again lots of stuff
New stuff:

ul.li: You can now right click on messages to see a context menu, showing various actions like forward, delete, copy (text, as markdown, image, links), select, message delivery info
You can select multiple message and do grouped actions on them
Messages can now receive reactions and user can send reactions and view them
Opening an unread message will open it at the starting of the last read message
If chat receives a message it will only be marked read when user scrolls down to it
Chat list now shows when somebody is typing

description.p: Fixed stuff:

ul.li: Favourited sticker from other devices will now automatically show up in favourites
Accent color won't dull now for lots of elements when unfocusing the window
Fixed a bug where small chats where being stuck to the top instead of bottom
Lots of small fixes

description.p: Lots of optimizations as well as new features
New stuff:

ul.li: You can send stickers now, fully featured sticker pane
Scrolling is now smoother and more kinetic, should feel natural
